name: Yaroslavl Oblast
summary_text: This division shows one regional deviation: the regional Investigative Committee opened a criminal case against LGBTQA+ activist Yaroslav Sirotkin for participation in an extremist organisation, based on 14 social-media posts and videos of 'propaganda of non-traditional sexual relationships' posted between December 2023 and January 2024 - illustrating how little conduct suffices under the federal extremism framework. Otherwise this division is covered by the dedicated country dossier: no further deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); assessed at the national score.

sources.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, June 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Home Office country policy and information note: sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, June 2025. LGB people generally do not face a real risk of persecution from the state solely for sexual orientation, but people in the North Caucasus, trans people, and publicly active LGBT+ advocates are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution. Same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned nationwide. The 'gay propaganda' law carries administrative fines or detention up to 15 days, escalating to criminal prosecution on repeat (up to 4 years); the 2023 'extremist' designation of the international LGBT+ movement allows support/activity to be classed extremist (2-6 years; organising 6-10 years). At least 139 people were impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws 2022-2024; official reporting is restricted and data limited.
